chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The divorce of the mute woman is that he takes her veil, places it upon her head, and then separates from her.
ai.seo_question: How is a divorce legally executed for a mute woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a pragmatic legal mechanism for the divorce of a mute woman, addressing the jurisprudential challenge of conveying the *talāq* formula without verbal articulation. By utilizing the physical act of placing the *miqna'ah* (a specific head covering) and subsequent withdrawal, the Imam demonstrates how Shia fiqh adapts ritual requirements to accommodate physical disabilities while maintaining the validity of the marital bond's dissolution.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A divorce of the mute is that he takes her veil, so he places it upon her head, and he takes it off’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Divorce by a speechless man can happen by his placing her headscarf on her head and then taking it away from her head.’”
